Name: opencode_instruction_hierarchy
Title: Do Coding Agents Actually Follow AGENTS.md? Testing Real Rules from Real Repos
Hypothesis: Coding agents running through real runtimes (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex CLI) fail to follow a significant fraction of rules in real-world AGENTS.md files, especially rules that go against model defaults or conflict with the runtime's own prompt.
Approach: 1. Pull real AGENTS.md files from popular GitHub repos (next.js, sentry, pydantic-ai, browser-use, etc.)
2. For each repo, identify rules that require the model to do something AGAINST its default behavior
3. Create coding tasks natural to each repo that test whether the agent follows those rules
4. Run tasks through coding agent runtimes and judge compliance
5. Compare: which rules break? Does the runtime matter? Does the model matter?
Key Design Principle: Only test rules where the model would do something DIFFERENT without the AGENTS.md. If a rule says 'use snake_case for SQL columns' and every model already does that by default, it's not a real test. Good tests: rules that contradict common conventions, require unusual patterns, or conflict with each other.
Runtimes: OpenCode: curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash && opencode run -m MODEL --format json -- 'task'
HOW TO RUN EXPERIMENTS: Use the actual coding agent CLI (opencode run, claude -p, codex exec) for generating responses.
Do NOT call model APIs directly (anthropic.Anthropic(), google.genai) — that bypasses the runtime.
API calls are fine for judging only.

Code References.notes: OpenCode source — study how it assembles AGENTS.md into prompts
